body.rationale: DECISION: Adopt the single analyst-motivated alternative - normalization='realized_volatility' with volatility_window=5 - and retain lookback=5, direction=1, max_absolute_daily_return=null. WHY ADOPT: price_profile shows cross-sectional dispersion in one-observation return SD (0.02520900080828789 for 300750.XSHE, 0.012242446444137979 for 600036.XSHG, 0.019867351566759856 for 601318.XSHG), and baseline five-observation scores inherit a symbol-specific scale (sample_sd_score 0.042777151396309596 / 0.027943663754569577 / 0.0402658932201447 in initial_inspection). Dividing each trailing return by its own trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(5) is the one motivated rescaling construct for a cross-symbol exploratory sample; per source_contract this 'does not make an annual Sharpe ratio or remove systematic risk', and no superiority or improved comparability is claimed - descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority. VOLATILITY_WINDOW=5: it reuses the same five daily returns already inside the five-observation lookback, so the trailing-observation requirement stays 6 closes per signal (the required window size is 5 returns built from 6 closes; it is not itself the warmup count) and eligibility/coverage is unchanged versus the baseline - the chosen-spec inspection (inspection_id 02046d95bdb2ac5f0a989096feb1f043f70a8f80a03f27395705da36ad07d596) reports for each symbol 62 observed closes, closes_required_per_signal=6, warmup_exclusions=5, additional_exclusions=0, eligible_signals=57, signals_with_next_observed_close=56. Larger allowed windows (6-20) would add warmup exclusions and shrink coverage on a 62-close sample without cited motivating evidence. RETAINED PARAMETERS: direction=1 and lookback=5 stay at baseline values because drift signs differ across symbols (mean one-observation returns -0.002168177418430765, +0.0007583228830076313, -0.0010854258683716392) and no forward labels exist, so no winning sign or lookback is established. max_absolute_daily_return stays null because a return bound would add an applicability exclusion and is not separately motivated; max absolute one-observation returns (0.07121171770972035 / 0.02537274391838862 / 0.06406368460955258) are descriptive only and justify no bound. UPDATED DEFINITION - name: 'Trailing close-return, realized-volatility-normalized (exploratory)'. expression: score[t] = 1 * (close[t]/close[t-5] - 1) / (SD5[t] * sqrt(5)), where SD5[t] is the sample SD (n-1) of the five daily close-to-close returns r[i] = close[i]/close[i-1] - 1 for i = t-4..t, using only observations at or before t. signal_rule: signal after close t; require 6 trailing observed closes (close[t-5] through close[t]) so the lookback and the 5-return volatility window are simultaneously satisfied; require positive SD5[t] when normalized; no extra return-magnitude eligibility exclusion (max_absolute_daily_return=null). availability_rule: use only observed closes at or before signal close t; the current historical download is not a vintage archive, so point-in-time availability is not established. execution_rule: no earlier than the next observed close after t; the last observed row (2026-07-31) has no execution observation; no tradability or performance claim. universe: 601318.XSHG, 600036.XSHG, 300750.XSHE; fixed convenience sample, not a point-in-time universe. input_units: unadjusted close in CNY/share; simple daily and trailing returns dimensionless; the normalized score is a dimensionless return/return ratio, not an annual Sharpe ratio. ASSUMPTIONS: sample SD divides by n-1; windows use past observed rows with no filling; the repeated 600036.XSHG close of 37.0 on 2026-05-26 and 2026-05-27 is an observed equality, not a missing or filled row; close-only jumps are not attributed to corporate actions - the 601318.XSHG 52.76 (2026-06-17) to 49.38 (2026-06-18) drop is an observed price change only, with no corporate-action handling claimed; the normalization is a fixed construct choice made before any forward evaluation, not a fitted parameter. COVERAGE AND SCORE-SCALE VS BASELINE: coverage is identical - per symbol 57 eligible signals and 56 with a next observed close, only the 5 warmup exclusions and 0 additional exclusions, so the single zero-return observation for 600036.XSHG still yields positive SD5[t] and no row is lost. All 171 eligible score rows (57 per symbol x 3 symbols) change value (changed_score_or_eligibility_rows_from_initial = 171 in the chosen-spec inspection; no eligibility rows changed): the scale moves from raw return to a volatility-scaled dimensionless quantity, e.g. mean_score -0.3889859692838746 (300750.XSHE), -0.28153524939007035 (600036.XSHG), -0.40783855957329596 (601318.XSHG) and sample_sd_score 1.125523331799228 / 1.7404777088984507 / 1.5579151612791153. This is a descriptive score-scale change only; it cannot establish superiority, improved comparability, alpha, removal of systematic risk or corporate-action handling. NEXT EVIDENCE NEEDED: forward return labels, together with transaction costs, volume, corporate-action records and point-in-time universe membership, in a separate independent evaluation; none exist in this frozen sample. INSPECTION STATUS: the inspection of this exact spec is descriptive only (scores/coverage on frozen rows; no backtest, no forward labels, no provider request, no proof the revision is better), and the supervisor's pre-review inspection of the same spec is likewise descriptive only.

body.rationale: DECISION: Adopt the single analyst-motivated alternative - normalization='realized_volatility' with volatility_window=5 - and retain lookback=5, direction=1, max_absolute_daily_return=null. WHY ADOPT: price_profile shows cross-sectional dispersion in one-observation return SD (0.02520900080828789 for 300750.XSHE, 0.012242446444137979 for 600036.XSHG, 0.019867351566759856 for 601318.XSHG), and baseline five-observation scores inherit a symbol-specific scale (sample_sd_score 0.042777151396309596 / 0.027943663754569577 / 0.0402658932201447 in initial_inspection). Dividing each trailing return by its own trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(5) is the one motivated rescaling construct for a cross-symbol exploratory sample; per source_contract this 'does not make an annual Sharpe ratio or remove systematic risk', and no superiority or improved comparability is claimed - descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority. VOLATILITY_WINDOW=5: it reuses the same five daily returns already inside the five-observation lookback, so the trailing-observation requirement stays 6 closes per signal (the required window size is 5 returns built from 6 closes; it is not itself the warmup count) and eligibility/coverage is unchanged versus the baseline - the chosen-spec inspection (inspection_id 02046d95bdb2ac5f0a989096feb1f043f70a8f80a03f27395705da36ad07d596) reports for each symbol 62 observed closes, closes_required_per_signal=6, warmup_exclusions=5, additional_exclusions=0, eligible_signals=57, signals_with_next_observed_close=56. Larger allowed windows (6-20) would add warmup exclusions and shrink coverage on a 62-close sample without cited motivating evidence. RETAINED PARAMETERS: direction=1 and lookback=5 stay at baseline values because drift signs differ across symbols (mean one-observation returns -0.002168177418430765, +0.0007583228830076313, -0.0010854258683716392) and no forward labels exist, so no winning sign or lookback is established. max_absolute_daily_return stays null because a return bound would add an applicability exclusion and is not separately motivated; max absolute one-observation returns (0.07121171770972035 / 0.02537274391838862 / 0.06406368460955258) are descriptive only and justify no bound. UPDATED DEFINITION - name: 'Trailing close-return, realized-volatility-normalized (exploratory)'. expression: score[t] = 1 * (close[t]/close[t-5] - 1) / (SD5[t] * sqrt(5)), where SD5[t] is the sample SD (n-1) of the five daily close-to-close returns r[i] = close[i]/close[i-1] - 1 for i = t-4..t, using only observations at or before t. signal_rule: signal after close t; require 6 trailing observed closes (close[t-5] through close[t]) so the lookback and the 5-return volatility window are simultaneously satisfied; require positive SD5[t] when normalized; no extra return-magnitude eligibility exclusion (max_absolute_daily_return=null). availability_rule: use only observed closes at or before signal close t; the current historical download is not a vintage archive, so point-in-time availability is not established. execution_rule: no earlier than the next observed close after t; the last observed row (2026-07-31) has no execution observation; no tradability or performance claim. universe: 601318.XSHG, 600036.XSHG, 300750.XSHE; fixed convenience sample, not a point-in-time universe. input_units: unadjusted close in CNY/share; simple daily and trailing returns dimensionless; the normalized score is a dimensionless return/return ratio, not an annual Sharpe ratio. ASSUMPTIONS: sample SD divides by n-1; windows use past observed rows with no filling; the repeated 600036.XSHG close of 37.0 on 2026-05-26 and 2026-05-27 is an observed equality, not a missing or filled row; close-only jumps are not attributed to corporate actions - the 601318.XSHG 52.76 (2026-06-17) to 49.38 (2026-06-18) drop is an observed price change only, with no corporate-action handling claimed; the normalization is a fixed construct choice made before any forward evaluation, not a fitted parameter. COVERAGE AND SCORE-SCALE VS BASELINE: coverage is identical - per symbol 57 eligible signals and 56 with a next observed close, only the 5 warmup exclusions and 0 additional exclusions, so the single zero-return observation for 600036.XSHG still yields positive SD5[t] and no row is lost. All 171 eligible score rows (57 per symbol x 3 symbols) change value (changed_score_or_eligibility_rows_from_initial = 171 in the chosen-spec inspection; no eligibility rows changed): the scale moves from raw return to a volatility-scaled dimensionless quantity, e.g. mean_score -0.3889859692838746 (300750.XSHE), -0.28153524939007035 (600036.XSHG), -0.40783855957329596 (601318.XSHG) and sample_sd_score 1.125523331799228 / 1.7404777088984507 / 1.5579151612791153. This is a descriptive score-scale change only; it cannot establish superiority, improved comparability, alpha, removal of systematic risk or corporate-action handling. NEXT EVIDENCE NEEDED: forward return labels, together with transaction costs, volume, corporate-action records and point-in-time universe membership, in a separate independent evaluation; none exist in this frozen sample. INSPECTION STATUS: the inspection of this exact spec is descriptive only (scores/coverage on frozen rows; no backtest, no forward labels, no provider request, no proof the revision is better), and the supervisor's pre-review inspection of the same spec is likewise descriptive only.
